title.en: Geography: India - Population, Transport, Communication and Trade

text.en: Asha saw a crowded train station. "How does India move so many people and goods?" she asked.

India's population is over a billion, spread unevenly, with the Ganga plains very dense. Density is the number of people per square km. Literacy and sex ratio are important measures.
Transport includes roads, railways, waterways and airways. The Golden Quadrilateral links the four metros, railways are the lifeline, and ports like Chennai and Mumbai handle sea trade. Communication includes the post, telephone, radio, TV and the internet.
Trade is the exchange of goods. India exports items such as textiles, IT services and engineering goods and imports petroleum and gold. The balance of trade is the difference between exports and imports.

Density is the number of people per square km.
Literacy and sex ratio are important measures.
Transport includes roads, railways, waterways and airways.
The Golden Quadrilateral links the four metros, railways are the lifeline, and ports like Chennai and Mumbai handle sea trade.
Communication includes the post, telephone, radio, TV and the internet.
Trade is the exchange of goods.
India exports items such as textiles, IT services and engineering goods and imports petroleum and gold.
India is home to over 1.21 billion people in the 2011 Census—nearly 17.5 percent of humanity living on just 2.4 percent of Earth's land.

board.text: India: 17.5% of world people on 2.4% land

text.en: Population distribution depends heavily on relief, water and soil: the flat alluvial Indo-Gangetic plain is packed, while cold Ladakh deserts and steep Himalayas are sparse.

board.text: Plains dense vs mountains & deserts sparse

text.en: India's average population density rose to 382 persons per square kilometre in 2011, led by states like Bihar (1,106) and West Bengal, while Arunachal Pradesh had just 17.
Geographers track three population trends: birth rate, death rate and migration—rural-to-urban moves for jobs fuel rapid city growth.
Sex ratio (943 females per 1,000 males in 2011) and overall literacy (74.04 percent) measure social well-being and gender equality.
Urbanisation reached 31.16 percent in 2011, creating mega-cities like Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata alongside traffic, housing and sanitation demands.
Transport acts as the circulatory system of the economy across four modes: land (road, rail, pipeline), water (inland & ocean) and air.

board.text: Four transport networks move people & goods

text.en: Roadways offer door-to-door flexibility through National Highways, State Highways, District Roads, rural PMGSY roads and Border Roads.
Two mega highway projects stand out: the 5,846 km Golden Quadrilateral linking Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, plus the North–South and East–West corridors.
Indian Railways operates Asia's largest rail network across gauges, carrying coal, grain, steel and millions of daily passengers reliably.

board.text: Indian Railways: Asia's largest rail grid

text.en: Suburban and Metro rails in Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai and Bengaluru ease city congestion while Konkan Railway conquers tough Western Ghats terrain.
Pipelines safely transport crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas—such as the Hazira–Vijaipur–Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline—with minimal spills.

board.text: Pipelines carry oil & natural gas safely

text.en: Waterways are the cheapest and cleanest mode for bulky cargo: National Waterways like Ganga NW-1 and Brahmaputra NW-2 serve inland trade.

board.text: Waterways: cheapest mode for heavy cargo

text.en: Along India's 7,516 km coast, major ports like Mumbai, JNPT, Kandla, Mormugao, Kochi, Chennai, Visakhapatnam and Kolkata handle international cargo.
Airways provide the fastest connection across mountains, oceans and North-East India, serving emergency relief and business travel.
Communication links people without physical travel: personal tools like mobile phones and email, and mass media like radio, TV and satellites.
Indian satellites like INSAT and IRS power weather forecasts, distance education, disaster warnings and high-speed digital connectivity.

board.text: INSAT & IRS satellites guide weather & data

text.en: Trade splits into internal trade within states and international trade across borders, measured carefully through exports and imports.
India exports software services, pharmaceuticals, refined petroleum, gems, textiles and engineering goods, while importing crude oil, machinery and gold.
Balance of trade equals exports minus imports: earning more from exports yields a favourable surplus, while exceeding imports creates a deficit.
To link the whole system together: healthy skilled citizens + fast roads/rails/ports + digital networks = strong internal and global trade.

board.text: People + transport + digital links = strong trade

text.en: Shifting heavy freight toward electrified rail and clean coastal shipping reduces fuel imports and cuts carbon emissions for India's future.

board.text: Cleaner rail & coastal shipping cut emissions

problem.en: How can India make its Balance of Trade more favourable while cutting transport costs?

text.en: Understand Balance of Trade.

why.en: Balance of Trade = value of Exports minus value of Imports; heavy crude oil imports often push India toward a trade deficit.

text.en: Lower logistics costs with transport.

why.en: Dedicated rail freight corridors, Golden Quadrilateral highways and fast port loading make Indian manufactured goods cheaper to export.

text.en: Grow high-value exports & clean energy.

why.en: Exporting IT services, medicines, vehicles and textiles while shifting trains and buses to solar/electric power cuts crude oil import bills.

prompt.en: A friend says Exports are goods bought from other countries. How will you reply?

points.en: Balance of trade = exports minus imports.
